thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated 5xx/error-rate spike affecting control-plane auth and org-lookup endpoints (us-west). Graphs: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/auth-5xx; alert threshold crossed at 1765432087. Pager duty: oncall-sre.

incident-bot: Relevant symptoms: 502/504 at the API gateway, increased backend 5xx from `auth-service` and `org-lookup` (latency also climbing). Ticket created: INC-2026-334.

sara: I'm on it. Pulling logs and recent deploys. Starting with last 30m of auth-service logs.

sara: `kubectl get deploy -n controlplane | grep auth-service` -> looked fine, no rollout in the last hour. Checking config push history.

ops-bot: Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/example/runbooks/control-plane-auth.md — recommended mitigations: enable fallback cache, route to standby cluster, disable aggressive TTL changes.

jia: Notified SRE and runtime teams. I'm looking at the rate of org lookup RPCs from the API gateway — saw a sudden 8x increase starting 1765432060. Could be a client loop.

sara: grabbing gateway logs now. Top endpoints hitting org-lookup: `/v1/projects/*/members` and `/v1/sessions/create`. Some clients are indeed retrying aggressively.

sara: quick mitigation: flipping feature flag `org_lookup_strict` to false to allow cached lookups. Doing feature flag flip now.

sara: `curl -X POST https://ff.redwood/flags/org_lookup_strict -d '{"enabled":false}'` -> 200 OK.

tabitha: Good call. Also bumping cache TTL on the local cache from 0s -> 30s in-flight via config override. Pushing: `envsubst < cache-override.yaml | kubectl apply -f -`

mike: Noted. Can we scale auth-service replicas while we investigate? Scaling to handle the spike.

sara: scaling auth-service from 3 -> 10 replicas in us-west. `kubectl scale deploy/auth-service --replicas=10 -n controlplane` -> started.

ops-bot: scaling noted. Also enabling circuit-breaker on gateway for org-lookup to avoid cascading failures.

alex: Quick check: any recent infra deploys or control-plane config pushes? I see a config change to caching defaults merged ~1765432005 by infra-team (lowered TTL to 0 for faster invalidation) — that seems suspicious.

jia: Confirmed. That PR is likely the trigger. Rolling it back would be the clean fix, but need cautious rollout.

sara: For immediate safety we reverted the TTL change in staging and are applying a conservative override in prod (30s). We'll plan a rollback of the PR once traffic stabilizes.

liz: Support update: Currently ~3.8% of API requests are returning 5xx globally; us-west spike ~12% for 20 minutes. Top impacted org: acme-inc (12% error rate on their token). No PII exposed. Messaging customers: preparing status page blurb.

sara: After cache TTL bump + feature-flag flip + scale + circuit-breaker, error-rate dropped from peak ~18% to ~2.5% over 12 minutes. Metrics: `5xx_rate: 0.18 -> 0.025` (us-west).

mike: Monitoring logs for signs of retries causing pressure. Adding firewall to block obvious retry loops from misbehaving clients? Might be heavy-handed.

tabitha: Instead, added gateway rate-limits for anonymous/unthrottled endpoints and added `Retry-After` guidance. Config applied.

sara: Handing off to mike for the next hour for watch & verify. I've captured commands and notes in INC-2026-334 and will join async. @mike please take over.

mike: Taking handoff. I'll keep an eye on error rates and the auth replica stabilization. If anything regresses, page me oncall.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place, severity downgraded to SEV-2 (degraded) at 1765432340. Continue monitoring for 60m.

jia: Postmortem notes (quick): root cause = aggressive cache TTL change (0s) merged without canary, which removed cache buffering and amplified client retry traffic into auth/org lookup backends. Contributing factor: no circuit-breaker on gateway for these lookups.

alex: Action items: (1) Revert TTL PR in prod with gradual canary; (2) Add pre-flight canary + synthetic load test for cache-related config changes; (3) Harden gateway circuit-breaker defaults; (4) Improve alerting to correlate sudden RPC rate jumps with deploy/config pushes.

liz: Support action: notify top affected customers with CTA + apology and mitigation summary. Draft ready for review in #support.

sara: Leaving a short runbook update pointer in the ticket. Also adding a watch for potential rollout of the config PR later today — block until canary tests pass.

mike: Acknowledged. I'll update channel if I see any regression. Night team oncall FYI.

incident-bot: Auto-note: next oncall handoff scheduled at 1765436000.

ops-bot: Incident demoted to monitoring-only at 1765432440. Keep the thread for postmortem items. :white_check_mark:

sara: Thanks team. Good catch on the TTL PR. Will follow up with a short postmortem doc and reference the metric panels to include in the RCA.

mike: Thanks all.
